title: Striking the Money a Member is Asked For to Clear Rider Premium Owed
content:
Memorandum of the premium accounting desk on the figure a member is asked for when they offer to clear the rider premium standing owed on one of the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders.

## 1. The figure

The money a member is asked for to clear the rider premium they owe is the rider premium charged that is counted, less the money counted as having reached the rider premium account, less the credits set off; the figure is rounded to the nearest cent and is never less than nothing.

## 2. The span the entries are counted over

The days of grace the rider held allows are reckoned into whole months at thirty days to the month, any part month being dropped, and a span of so many months runs back over that many whole calendar months from the handling date, an entry posted in an earlier calendar month falling outside it; this bears on which entries are counted and not on whether the days of grace have run out.

## 3. The three sums

**The rider premium charged that is counted** is the rider premium charges posted to the rider premium account within the days of grace the rider held allows.

**The money counted as having reached the rider premium account** is the money posted to it within those same days of grace.

**The credits set off** are the credits posted to the rider premium account within those same days of grace.

## 4. The medical plan bill

The money left over on the medical plan bill is taken over every bill raised on the medical plan enrollment the rider hangs on. The money left over on the medical plan bill is what has been paid on it less the medical plan premium charged on it over the same span, and is never less than nothing. Nothing of it is carried to the rider premium account. The money counted as having reached the rider premium account is the money posted to that account alone.

## Worked through on hypothetical inputs

Take a rider allowing 60 days of grace, handled in a given month.

1. Sixty days reckoned at thirty days to the month gives a span of 2 whole months; the span runs back over the 2 whole calendar months ending with the month of handling, and an entry posted in an earlier calendar month falls outside it.
2. Within that span the rider premium account carries charges of 28.60 USD and 28.60 USD, so the rider premium charged that is counted is 57.20 USD.
3. Within the same span the account carries one payment of 20.00 USD, so the money counted as having reached it is 20.00 USD.
4. Within the same span the account carries one credit of 5.00 USD, so the credits set off come to 5.00 USD.
5. The money left over on the medical plan bill is what has been paid on that enrollment's bills less the medical plan premium charged on them; it is not carried to the rider premium account.
6. The money the member is asked for is 57.20 USD less 20.00 USD less 5.00 USD, that is **32.20 USD**.

Had those entries come to less than nothing between them, the figure asked for would be nothing. Every figure above is a hypothetical input.
